closingKeywordWhy: The PR ships the MVP the lane brief scoped: the stack-trace path (brief, compose authoring, verify) usable end to end. The issue also asks for harness postmortem-record intake where one exists, and a comment proposes SARIF/security-finding intake. Neither is built here, so this is Refs #614 with those named as follow-ups.
assumptions: Brainstorming sign-off was taken autonomously (fleet lane default): approach A (deterministic brief + verify, authoring composed by the skill) and decisions D1-D10 were self-answered with the recommended option. No fork was parked; none changes what the tool claims.
D2: reproduced requires a non-zero exit AND the signature (first line of the error message, or the error type when the message is empty, labelled type-only) in the ANSI-stripped runner output.

Review amendments (harness-code-review requested changes: 1 critical, 5 important): signatures are matched on an error line anchored by the brief's error type, not as a bare substring; generic type-only signatures (Error/Exception) are unverified; --expect needs 8+ characters; a signal death is unverified; the test and its sibling files under tests/generated/ are checked (escapes undone) for a quoted signature; the parser takes the error line that owns the frames; dist-packages/lib/pythonX frames are external and suffix matches keep 2+ segments; framework order is --framework, brief, extension. Recorded as A1-A5 in the spec.

D4: collection errors (vitest/playwright 'no tests', pytest exits 2-5), timeouts (124), 127, spawn errors, an executor throw, and an unknown framework are all 'unverified — could not reproduce', exit 3.

D6: verify only runs a file whose realpath is under <root>/tests/generated/ (exit 2 otherwise, nothing spawned). Containment is reimplemented in the engine because ts/src/mcp-server.ts (entry layer) is not importable from analysis.

D9: framework comes from --framework, then the extension (.py pytest, .spec/.e2e playwright, other JS/TS vitest), then the brief. Execution goes through deps.makeExecutor() (CanaryTestExecutor and the framework registry). Default --timeout is 60s.
A trace with frames but no error line abstains rather than inventing a signature. Java/Go/Ruby/.NET traces abstain and are named.
The skills README count was already stale at (29); it now reads the real directory count (33).

Execution was delegated to harness-planner and harness-task-executor, per autopilot. The review-driven amendment (source-echo guard and runner-output tail) and the ratchet task (12) were done by the lane itself.

Arch: module-size 48452 -> 49675 (+1223) against merge base 16b70424 (re-measured after rebasing past #613 and after the review fixes), measured on both trees with harness check-arch --json (CLI 12.10.1). An allowance was added and the floor refreshed with scripts/refresh-arch-baseline.mjs; violationIds were untouched. Entropy 141 vs 141 and perf delta OK (216 vs 214, the two new findings are the two CLI files' coupling ratios, covered by the ts/src/**/cli.ts coupling allowance; the verify subcommand was split into judomaster-verify-cli.ts to stay under the 300-line file threshold), both run through the repo's ratchet scripts against a detached base worktree. No entryPoints were added and maxFindings was not touched.
Shared lists (READINESS_COMMANDS, EXPECTED_COMMANDS, skills README, guides index, CHANGELOG) got append-only edits, because lane D (#613 canary-question) edits the same lists concurrently.
The roadmap row stays 'planned' with its spec and plan linked, because the PR is Refs and does not close the issue.

Deferred review suggestions (follow-ups, not built): V8 [cause] and CPython chained-exception boundaries in the brief (S6); running the runner with cwd=--root instead of the process cwd (S3, documented instead: run verify from the repo root; npx --yes may fetch the runner); a warning when the test mocks the suspect module; root '/' containment edge case (S5).
